also: my hair is standing on end

terms.gloss: the hairs stand up: have goosebumps
terms.grammar: horreō, horrēre, horruī with pilī as subject; the person in the dative (mihi)
evidence: Varr. LL 6.49: cum etiam in corpore pilī, ut arista in spīcā hordeī, horrent
terms.comment: Latin says this with a verb: the hairs on the body horrent, stand up and bristle, as Varro says they do when someone shivers hard, like the awn on an ear of barley.

terms.gloss: bristle up, come out in goosebumps; shiver
evidence: Cels. 1.3: frīgida pōtiō inūtilis est iīs quī facile inhorrēscunt (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 10.116: gallīnae inhorrēscunt ēditō ōvō excutiuntque sēsē (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: a shudder, a chill that runs over the whole body
evidence: Cels. 3.3: horrōrem, ubi tōtum corpus intremit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The shiver rather than the bumps: Celsus calls it frīgus when the hands and feet grow cold, horror when the whole body shakes.

evidence: Vulg. Sir. 27.15: loquella multum jūrāns horripilātiōnem capitī statuet

phrases.latin: cum etiam in corpore pilī, ut arista in spīcā hordeī, horrent
phrases.english: when even the hairs on the body stand up, like the awn on an ear of barley

phrases.latin: gallīnae inhorrēscunt ēditō ōvō excutiuntque sēsē
phrases.english: when they have laid an egg, hens ruffle up and shake themselves

sources: Lewis & Short: horreo · Lewis & Short: inhorresco · Lewis & Short: horror · Lewis & Short: horripilatio
